references.text: God fills Bezalel with His Spirit, with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge, showing that God equips His chosen ones with His Spirit for special tasks – parallel to Pharaoh’s recognition of God’s Spirit in Joseph.
The Lord points out Joshua as a man with the Spirit in him, which parallels Pharaoh’s acknowledgment of God’s Spirit in Joseph and shows God’s selection of leaders through His Spirit.

The queen tells King Belshazzar that Daniel has 'the spirit of the holy gods' within him – nearly identical wording and situation to when Pharaoh recognized God’s Spirit in Joseph. Both are pagan rulers who recognize divine empowerment.
Daniel excelled above the others because 'an extraordinary spirit was in him,' paralleling how Pharaoh recognized the divine spirit in Joseph.
The seven men chosen to serve must be full of the Spirit and wisdom, showing that recognizing God’s Spirit in a person is a criterion for selection to service.
Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, sees God’s glory – an example of how God’s Spirit rests upon chosen individuals, just as Pharaoh recognized God’s Spirit in Joseph.
Thematic parallel concerning 'the man of God' who carries divine wisdom and guidance during an early crisis.
Parallel about leaders (Pharaoh and Jehoshaphat) who actively seek a man with God’s Spirit or prophetic gift for guidance.
Repetition of candidate 4: Parallel about leaders seeking prophetic guidance in times of crisis.
